mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4% combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) over three months signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% and PAYEMS declines for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4% and PAYEMS declines for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% signals a strong demand environment, which supports corporate earnings growth and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 rises by more than 3% year-over-year.
